decision: N8 uses M=1024 and 2048, and N9 uses the first 32768 WikiText2 test tokens per tokenizer in 1024-token windows.
evidence: Application-specific config and protocol refine the overarching N8 placeholder M=512/2048 before any N8 execution.
implications: N5–N7 frozen configuration and held-out shapes remain unchanged. Scored next-token count is 32x1023; exact tokenizer, text and token hashes are archived. Independent official Transformers forward qualification precedes model quality claims.
rationale: Align layer geometry with actual context windows and replace the historical short repeated-token proxy with fixed natural text.

decision: Freeze independent implementation and model-quality gates before N9 model outputs are measured.
evidence: Official Transformers CPU BF16 reference: first64 fixed tokens; native qualification finite, logit relative L2<=0.03, meanKL<=0.01, absNLLdelta<=0.05, top1>=0.90. Candidate versus qualified same-run native: absNLLdelta<=0.01, meanKL<=0.02, top1>=0.97 and all finite.
implications: Failed native qualification blocks long-form quality claims. Failed candidate quality makes its timings ineligible as a successful speedup. All metrics and failures are retained; thresholds cannot be relaxed after seeing outcomes.
rationale: Separate correctness of the reconstructed native forward from quality effects of replacing its matmuls.

decision: Keep both complete-call and prepared-kernel eligibility requirements when selecting N5 winners, including candidates that compile in only one scope.
evidence: Early N5-screen rows retain prepared-kernel VMEM failures on 2048x2048x512 candidates; successful call rows remain separately visible.
implications: This conservative bounded study may exclude a useful call-only candidate. No post-hoc relaxation or replacement is made; infeasibility remains a result rather than a numerical error.
rationale: The largest tiles can fit after complete-call compiler simplification yet exceed the 48MiB VMEM limit for a standalone prepared kernel. The requirement was fixed before this screen.

decision: Add four N8 cases at M=512 for Mistral7B and Qwen32B gate/up and down geometry, alongside the 12 main M=1024/2048 cases.
evidence: Pre-execution inspection of build_application_campaign_v001.py groups and frozen N5 training_shape_ids; this is based on dimension coverage, not observed speedups.
implications: This amends D006 only by adding four anchor cases before N8 configuration/execution. N5/N7 shapes and measurements remain frozen. N9 still uses the 1024-token cases for its policies.
rationale: The main application shapes have no exact overlap with N5 LLM tuning, so the selected-MM controls would otherwise never run. The added gate/up shapes connect N5 tuned controls directly to N8 fusion ablations.

decision: Freeze the N6a selector from fresh N5 confirmation before any held-out N7 timings.

decision: Preserve the first N6 execution as a profiling diagnostic failure and investigate a versioned recovery.
evidence: Run20260919T063959Z-N6-v5e-v004-d93a61, commitf6cd867c2ef0e92477f21034123e5baa59062ef4; profile_successful_captures=0.
implications: Do not make device-utilization or overlap claims from this run. Keep its complete archive and compiler diagnostics; any recovery uses a new code version and execution directory.
rationale: All 18 ordinary timing checks passed, but all 18 captured trace files lacked an identifiable TPU process. Successful process exit does not establish usable profiling evidence.

decision: Correct the N6 profiler mode in a new recovery wrapper to TRACE_COMPUTE_AND_SYNC with device tracing enabled.
evidence: Archived N6 run20260919T063959Z-N6-v5e-v004-d93a61; official JAX profiling documentation and prior verified same-version profiling plan under strassen-tpu/evidence/validation/2026-09-11-v5e-profiling/plan.json.
implications: Preserve the original campaign, failed traces and executed code. Record the profiler-only override explicitly in the recovery archive. Keep algorithm choices, matrix inputs, allocation, ordinary timing policy and trace-validation criteria fixed.
rationale: The frozen N6 campaign mistakenly requested TRACE_ONLY, which is not a documented JAX TPU trace mode. The resulting files contain only host events. The strict analyzer correctly refused to interpret them as TPU measurements.

decision: Proceed with full Qwen and Mistral checkpoint preparation and the unchanged resident official CPU reference.
evidence: Run20260919T064658Z-N9-host-preflight-v5e-v004-39d3e0, commit933adbb71806f4db459f8781d0dee9bc01b2769c; resources.json and feasibility.json include visible cgroup limits and per-filesystem free capacity.
implications: No disk-offload implementation or threshold change is needed based on measured capacity. Preparation remains sequential while TPU timing is idle; actual reference execution failures, if any, will be archived and recovered in new versions.
rationale: An idle-host preflight measured about42.7GiB conservative available host memory and205.5GiB free disk, exceeding the predeclared20GiB Mistral reference memory estimate and21.9GiB input/tools disk estimate.

decision: Report ordinary complete-call latency and profiled device duration as separate findings, without a device-speedup claim from host-call wins.
evidence: Recovered N6 run20260919T064743Z-N6-v5e-v004-e7bc5e:18 validcaptures/144 modules. For vary-M representative, native/cubic/Strassen traced module means approximately0.359/0.420/0.392ms.
implications: Preserve the preregistered N7 evaluation and report limitations transparently. Treat the modeled HBM lower-bound field as an assumption-based traffic estimate; a warm small-M trace undercuts it, so it is not a validated hardware bound or utilization measurement.
rationale: The corrected N6 traces show native XLA faster on-device for all three representatives, despite custom-kernel advantages in some ordinary calls. Profiling may perturb execution and these scopes cannot establish a sole dispatch-overhead explanation.

decision: Preserve the failed model-tools environment and repair input preparation in a new environment and continuation driver.
